processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: System modified to synthesize five different alloys in one operation; five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace, successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks were hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.

processing_steps.method: reheating and water quenching, then cutting
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Aging was conducted in air at 450 °C, 500 °C, 550 °C and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h at each temperature, followed by oil quenching; this sample is the 500 °C / 24 h condition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 μm and some retained microsegregations of Mn (base state after hot rolling and water quenching); austenitic (fcc) structure expected for this composition.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: specimens prepared from segments by package spark erosion
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

ultimate_tensile_strength.uncertainty: approximate range for the 6Al alloy across aging conditions (not a per-condition value)

elongation.uncertainty: approximate range for the 6Al alloy across aging conditions (not a per-condition value)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.key_findings: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-sections prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl series, alloys with Al additions of 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening). [b0024]

The 6 wt.% Al variant is an intermediate Al variant: its mechanical data fall between those of the Al-free material and the 8 wt.% Al material, and it does not show equivalent mechanical properties to the ~8 wt.% Al variant. [b0024][b0025]

The pronounced aging strengthening observed in the 30 wt.% Mn system is attributed to the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides during aging, mainly for high (~8 wt.%) Al; the intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior. [b0025]

From Fig. 1, the Fe-Mn-Al-C density-reduction trend indicates a mass density of about 7.15 g/cm³ near 6 wt.% Al (approximate, read from figure; no measured density is reported specifically for Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al). [figure_001]

Aging at 500–600 °C in this alloy class is described as reducing mechanical twinning with strain hardening essentially associated to κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening; however, for the 6 wt.% Al intermediate alloy the aging effect on tensile behavior is reported to be small. [b0031][b0025]
